sm-noma.b: Montana Avenue north to the city line at the canyon rim, Ocean Avenue to 26th Street
sm-noma.d: Santa Monica's estate grid: wide, tree-lined numbered streets of large single-family homes, with Montana Avenue's shops at the bottom and San Vicente's coral-tree median running through. It is the only Santa Monica neighborhood with its own private patrol.

sm-gold-coast.b: The beachfront strip along Palisades Beach Road, below the Palisades Park bluffs
sm-gold-coast.d: A single row of houses on the sand north of the pier, many dating to the studio era of the 1920s and 30s. Lots back straight onto the beach, with the Annenberg Community Beach House in the middle.

sm-wilmont.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Montana Avenue, Ocean Avenue to 26th Street
sm-wilmont.d: Condos and small apartment buildings near the ocean that give way to single-family streets as you head east toward 26th. Walkable to Montana Avenue, Wilshire and Downtown.

sm-northeast.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Montana Avenue east of 26th Street, to the Los Angeles line
sm-northeast.d: A small, quiet pocket of single-family homes and low-rise condos on the Brentwood border, with Santa Monica schools and city services.

sm-downtown.b: Ocean Avenue to Lincoln Boulevard, Wilshire Boulevard to Pico Boulevard
sm-downtown.d: The Third Street Promenade, the pier, the Expo line terminus and the Civic Center. Mostly condos, lofts and rentals, a few blocks from the sand.

sm-midcity.b: Lincoln Boulevard to the city line, Wilshire Boulevard to Olympic Boulevard
sm-midcity.d: Santa Monica's medical and commercial middle, with both of the city's hospitals and a mix of condos, apartments and single-family streets.

sm-pico.b: Olympic Boulevard to Pico Boulevard, Lincoln Boulevard to Centinela Avenue
sm-pico.d: Virginia Avenue Park and the Bergamot arts district anchor this mixed pocket of bungalows, duplexes and apartments between the freeway and Pico.

sm-ocean-park.b: Pico Boulevard to the Venice line, the beach to Lincoln Boulevard
sm-ocean-park.d: Main Street's shops, Ocean Park Boulevard and walk-street cottages near the sand. Small lots, Craftsman bungalows and modern rebuilds sit side by side.

sm-sunset-park.b: Pico Boulevard to the city line, Lincoln Boulevard east to the airport
sm-sunset-park.d: Santa Monica's family pocket: blocks of 1940s and 50s single-family homes around Clover Park and the airport, with Ocean Park Boulevard's cafes and Santa Monica schools.

brw-park.b: San Vicente Boulevard to Sunset Boulevard, 26th Street and Allenford Avenue to Cliffwood Avenue
brw-park.d: Brentwood's estate grid, laid out around landscaped traffic circles. Big flat lots behind tall hedges, with the Brentwood Country Mart at the corner.

brw-park-north.name: Brentwood Park North of Sunset
brw-park-north.b: North of Sunset Boulevard around Rockingham, Bristol and Oakmont
brw-park-north.d: Estate streets climbing just above Sunset, with larger hillside lots, gated drives and canyon views over the original Brentwood Park.

brw-flats.b: San Vicente Boulevard to Sunset Boulevard, Cliffwood Avenue to Barrington Avenue
brw-flats.d: Gently sloping streets of traditional and new-build homes between San Vicente's coral trees and Brentwood Village, the walkable cluster of shops at Sunset and Barrington.

brw-glen.b: Sunset Boulevard to the VA grounds, west of the 405
brw-glen.d: A tight grid of smaller-lot single-family homes tucked between the VA campus and the freeway, a short walk from Brentwood Village.

brw-terrace.b: San Vicente Boulevard to Montana Avenue, the Santa Monica line to Bundy Drive
brw-terrace.d: Single-family streets wrapped around the Brentwood Country Club golf course, right on the Santa Monica border.

brw-south.b: Montana Avenue to Wilshire Boulevard, the Santa Monica line to Bundy Drive
brw-south.d: A transitional strip of single-family homes, duplexes and condos between Brentwood and Santa Monica, close to Wilshire's offices and shops.

brw-corridor.name: San Vicente Condo Corridor
brw-corridor.b: San Vicente Boulevard to Wilshire Boulevard, Bundy Drive to Barrington Avenue
brw-corridor.d: Brentwood's condo district: mid-rise buildings and townhomes behind San Vicente's restaurant row, the most common way into a Brentwood address.

brw-mandeville.b: Mandeville Canyon Road and every street off it, from Sunset to the end of the canyon
brw-mandeville.d: A long, wooded canyon with a country feel, horse properties and big lots. Mandeville Canyon Road is one of the longest dead-end streets in the city.

brw-kenter.b: Kenter Avenue and the Crestwood Hills streets above it
brw-kenter.d: Hillside homes in the canyon above Kenter Canyon Elementary, including Crestwood Hills, a postwar cooperative tract of modernist houses.

brw-bundy.b: North Bundy Drive and the streets off it, up toward Mount St. Mary's
brw-bundy.d: Hillside streets off Bundy Drive north of Sunset, climbing toward the Mount St. Mary's Chalon campus and the Getty ridge.

brw-tigertail.b: Tigertail Road and its side streets north of Sunset
brw-tigertail.d: A narrow canyon of hillside homes off Tigertail Road, with mid-century houses and large rebuilds on view lots.

brw-heights.name: Brentwood Heights
brw-heights.b: North of Sunset between Barrington Avenue and the 405
brw-heights.d: Hillside streets climbing from Brentwood Village toward the Getty, including gated Brentwood Circle and the Westgate Heights streets.

pal-castellammare.b: The hillside above Pacific Coast Highway where Sunset meets the coast
pal-castellammare.d: Italian-named streets stacked on the bluff above PCH, with Mediterranean villas and ocean views from almost every lot. Much of it is rebuilding after the 2025 fire.

pal-miramar.b: Paseo Miramar and the streets off it, above Sunset near PCH
pal-miramar.d: A steep hillside enclave reached by one winding road, with big ocean and canyon views and a trailhead to Parker Mesa at the top.

pal-highlands.b: Palisades Drive north of Sunset, up Santa Ynez Canyon
pal-highlands.d: A planned 1970s and 80s community up Santa Ynez Canyon, with newer homes, townhouses and gated enclaves surrounded by Topanga State Park.

pal-marquez.b: North of Sunset between El Medio and Palisades Drive
pal-marquez.d: Postwar ranch houses and newer view homes on the slope above Sunset, with a small shopping strip at Marquez Avenue and ocean views on many streets. Much of it is rebuilding after the 2025 fire.

pal-upper-bienveneda.name: Upper Bienveneda & El Medio
pal-upper-bienveneda.b: North of Sunset between Marquez Knolls and Temescal Canyon
pal-upper-bienveneda.d: Hillside streets off Bienveneda and upper El Medio with some of the biggest ocean views in the Palisades, just above Palisades Charter High School.

pal-alphabet.b: North of Sunset, east of the Village, below Temescal Gateway Park
pal-alphabet.d: The original 1920s Palisades, laid out on streets named alphabetically for Methodist missionaries. Narrow streets and small lots, walkable to the Village, and rebuilding after the 2025 fire.

pal-upper-riviera.b: North of Sunset around Amalfi Drive
pal-upper-riviera.d: Winding streets above the Riviera Country Club with large hillside lots, privacy and canyon views, bordering Brentwood and Will Rogers State Historic Park.

pal-elmedio-bluffs.b: South of Sunset from Temescal Canyon west to Las Casas
pal-elmedio-bluffs.d: A mesa of single-family homes on the bluff above PCH, with ocean views along the rim streets.

pal-via-bluffs.b: South of Sunset between Temescal Canyon and Potrero Canyon
pal-via-bluffs.d: Bluff-top streets named for colleges, a short walk south of the Village, with ocean views along the edge.

pal-village.name: The Village
pal-village.b: Sunset Boulevard's commercial core around Swarthmore and Via de la Paz
pal-village.d: The Palisades' downtown: Palisades Village shops, the Village Green and a grid of homes and condos within walking distance of everything.

pal-huntington.name: The Huntington
pal-huntington.b: South of Sunset between Potrero Canyon and Chautauqua Boulevard
pal-huntington.d: Wide, walkable streets of large homes on the bluff, close to the Village and the beach. One of the most sought-after pockets on the Westside.

pal-lower-riviera.b: South of Sunset around the Riviera Country Club
pal-lower-riviera.d: Large homes on Napoli Drive and the streets ringing the Riviera golf course, where the Napoli rim lots look straight over the fairways.

pal-rustic.b: The canyon floor along Latimer and Brooktree roads
pal-rustic.d: A wooded creek canyon of rustic homes and sycamores around Rustic Canyon Park, hidden below Sunset.

pal-smcanyon.b: Entrada Drive, Channel Road and the canyon streets above the beach
pal-smcanyon.d: A canyon pocket a block from the sand, with Channel Road's restaurants, older beach cottages and hillside homes, all in the City of LA.

bh-flats.b: Santa Monica Boulevard north to Sunset Boulevard, Doheny Drive west to the city line
bh-flats.d: The classic Beverly Hills flats: wide palm and jacaranda streets of large homes on big lots, a short walk to the Golden Triangle and Beverly Gardens Park.

bh-gt.b: Wilshire Boulevard, Santa Monica Boulevard and Canon Drive
bh-gt.d: The Golden Triangle: Rodeo Drive, Canon Drive and the city's retail and office core, with a small number of condos and apartments.

bh-east.b: South of Santa Monica Boulevard to Wilshire, east of Canon Drive to the city line
bh-east.d: Smaller lots than the flats north of Santa Monica Boulevard, mixing single-family homes, duplexes and low-rise apartments a few blocks from the Golden Triangle.

bh-south.b: South of Wilshire Boulevard to the city line
bh-south.d: South Beverly Hills: tree-lined grids of single-family homes, duplexes and apartments around Roxbury Park and La Cienega Park, served by the Beverly Hills schools.

bh-trousdale.b: The hillside streets around Loma Vista Drive and Trousdale Place above Sunset
bh-trousdale.d: Trousdale Estates: mid-century view homes on flat pads cut into the hills, with gated drives and city-to-ocean views.

bh-north.b: Hillside streets north of Sunset inside the city line, around Lexington Road and Benedict Canyon's mouth
bh-north.d: The Beverly Hills side of the canyons north of Sunset: large estates on winding streets, still inside city limits and city services.

bel-east-gate.b: Bel Air's streets entered from the East Gate on Sunset, around Bel Air Road
bel-east-gate.d: East Gate Old Bel Air: the original estate section, with large walled properties on curving streets just above Sunset.

bel-west-gate.b: Bel Air's streets entered from the West Gate, around Stone Canyon and the Bel-Air Country Club
bel-west-gate.d: West Gate Bel Air: estates around the Hotel Bel-Air, Stone Canyon and the country club fairways.

bel-upper.b: The upper streets of Bel Air north of the country club toward Mulholland
bel-upper.d: Upper Bel Air: hillside homes on ridges and canyon streets with long views, quieter and more varied in size than the lower gates.

bel-roscomare.b: Roscomare Road and the Bel Air Crest streets toward Mulholland
bel-roscomare.d: Roscomare Valley and Bel Air Crest: a canyon of mid-century and remodeled homes with its own school, plus the gated Bel Air Crest community up top.

bel-beverly-glen.b: The streets off Beverly Glen Boulevard between Sunset and Mulholland
bel-beverly-glen.d: Beverly Glen: a canyon of hillside homes ranging from small cabins to new builds, with a small village of shops at the top.

bel-holmby.d: The north-of-Sunset part of Holmby Hills: very large estates on deep lots next to Bel Air's East Gate.

bhpo-benedict.b: The streets off Benedict Canyon Drive above the Beverly Hills city line
bhpo-benedict.d: Benedict Canyon: a long canyon of hillside homes on side streets and ridges, with a Beverly Hills mailing address and City of LA services.

bhpo-franklin.b: The streets off Franklin Canyon and upper Beverly Drive
bhpo-franklin.d: Franklin Canyon and upper Beverly Drive: wooded canyon lots near Franklin Canyon Park, between Coldwater and Benedict.

bhpo-coldwater.b: The streets off Coldwater Canyon Drive between Beverly Hills and Mulholland
bhpo-coldwater.d: Coldwater Canyon: hillside homes along the canyon and its side streets, a main route between Beverly Hills and Studio City.

bhpo-beverly-park.b: The gated Beverly Park community off Mulholland
bhpo-beverly-park.d: Beverly Park: a guard-gated enclave of very large estates on the ridge, among the most exclusive addresses in Los Angeles.

bhpo-summitridge.b: Summitridge Drive and the streets around it between Benedict and Coldwater
bhpo-summitridge.d: Summitridge: ridge-top streets of view homes between Benedict and Coldwater canyons.

bhpo-doheny-estates.b: The hillside streets north of Sunset around Doheny Road and La Collina Drive
bhpo-doheny-estates.d: Doheny Estates and La Collina: view homes just above the Sunset Strip and the Beverly Hills flats.

hh-bird-streets.b: The streets named for birds above Sunset, west of Sunset Plaza
hh-bird-streets.d: The Bird Streets: Oriole, Thrasher, Blue Jay and their neighbors, steep streets of modern view homes above the Strip and among the most sought after in the hills.

hh-sunset-plaza.b: The streets off Sunset Plaza Drive above the Strip
hh-sunset-plaza.d: Sunset Plaza: view homes reached from Sunset Plaza Drive, close to the Strip's restaurants.

hh-west.b: The hillside streets above the Strip between Sunset Plaza and Laurel Canyon
hh-west.d: Hollywood Hills West: winding view streets just above West Hollywood.

hh-laurel.b: Laurel Canyon Boulevard and its side streets between Sunset and Mulholland
hh-laurel.d: Laurel Canyon: wooded canyon streets of cottages, remodels and new builds, centered on the Canyon Country Store.

hh-wonderland.b: The streets off Wonderland Avenue and Lookout Mountain
hh-wonderland.d: Wonderland Park: a side canyon off Laurel Canyon with its own elementary school.

hh-mt-olympus.b: The Mount Olympus development off Laurel Canyon
hh-mt-olympus.d: Mount Olympus: a planned hilltop neighborhood of mostly 1960s and 1970s view homes on streets named for Greek myths.

hh-nichols.b: Nichols Canyon Road and its side streets
hh-nichols.d: Nichols Canyon: a quiet, green canyon of hillside homes between Laurel Canyon and Outpost.

hh-outpost.b: Outpost Drive and the Outpost Estates streets above Franklin
hh-outpost.d: Outpost Estates: a 1920s Spanish Revival hillside tract with underground utilities and view homes above Hollywood.

hh-hollywood-heights.b: The hillside streets above Franklin near Highland and the Hollywood Bowl
hh-hollywood-heights.d: Hollywood Heights: older hillside homes and small apartment buildings close to the Bowl.

hh-whitley.b: The Whitley Heights streets above Franklin and the Hollywood Freeway
hh-whitley.d: Whitley Heights: a historic district of 1920s Mediterranean homes on narrow streets, an early hillside enclave of the film industry.

hh-cahuenga.b: The hillside streets on both sides of the Cahuenga Pass
hh-cahuenga.d: Cahuenga Pass: hillside homes along the pass between Hollywood and the Valley, quick to both.

hh-dell.b: The hillside streets north of Franklin between Cahuenga and Beachwood
hh-dell.d: The Hollywood Dell: a pocket of hillside homes and small buildings tucked above Franklin, close to Lake Hollywood.

hh-lake-hollywood.b: The streets ringing the Hollywood Reservoir
hh-lake-hollywood.d: Lake Hollywood Estates: homes around the reservoir and its walking loop, with views of the Hollywood Sign.

hh-beachwood.b: Beachwood Drive and its side streets up to the Hollywoodland gates
hh-beachwood.d: Beachwood Canyon: a canyon of 1920s and later homes below the Hollywood Sign, with Beachwood Village's market and cafe.

hh-hollywoodland.b: The Hollywoodland streets above the stone gates on Beachwood Drive
hh-hollywoodland.d: Hollywoodland: the original 1920s development the Hollywood Sign was built to advertise, with stone retaining walls and storybook homes.

ww-village.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Le Conte Avenue, Gayley Avenue to Hilgard Avenue
ww-village.d: Westwood Village: the shopping and dining district at UCLA's front door, with apartments and condos.

ww-north.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Sunset, Veteran Avenue to Gayley Avenue
ww-north.d: North Westwood: apartments and condos west of campus, plus single-family streets near Veteran Avenue.

ww-little-holmby.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Sunset, Hilgard Avenue to Beverly Glen Boulevard
ww-little-holmby.d: Little Holmby: a small grid of large homes between campus and Holmby Hills, among the most sought after streets in Westwood.

ww-holmby-westwood.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Santa Monica Boulevard, Westwood Boulevard to Beverly Glen
ww-holmby-westwood.d: Holmby-Westwood: single-family streets south of Wilshire's condo corridor, close to the Village and Century City.

ww-wilshire-west.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Santa Monica Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard to Westwood Boulevard
ww-wilshire-west.d: The blocks south of the Village: a mix of apartments, condos and some single-family homes near the Westwood Library.

ww-south.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Pico, Sepulveda Boulevard to Beverly Glen
ww-south.d: Westwood south of Santa Monica Boulevard: single-family streets around Westwood Park and the Westside Pavilion, plus apartments near the boulevards.

cen-core.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Pico, Century Park West to Century Park East
cen-core.d: The Century City core: office towers, the Westfield mall and high-rise condos.

cen-west.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Pico, Beverly Glen to Century Park West
cen-west.d: Century City's west side: condo towers and low-rise buildings near the Los Angeles Country Club and Beverly Glen.

cen-east.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Pico, Century Park East to the Beverly Hills line
cen-east.d: Century City's east side: condo buildings and apartments between the towers and Beverly Hills.

wla-sawtelle.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Pico, Bundy Drive to the 405
wla-sawtelle.d: Sawtelle: Japantown's restaurant row on Sawtelle Boulevard plus streets of apartments, small homes and newer townhomes.

wla-west.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Pico, the 405 to Sepulveda
wla-west.d: West LA east of the 405: apartments and modest single-family streets between Westwood and the freeway.

wla-south.b: Pico Boulevard to National, Bundy Drive to Sepulveda
wla-south.d: West LA south of Pico: single-family streets and apartments near the Expo Line and Westside Pavilion.

chv-rancho.b: Pico Boulevard to National, Sepulveda to Beverly Glen and Motor
chv-rancho.d: Rancho Park: single-family streets around the Rancho Park golf course and Cheviot Hills Recreation Center.

chv-cheviot.b: Pico Boulevard to National, Motor Avenue to Beverwil Drive and Castle Heights
chv-cheviot.d: Cheviot Hills: curving streets of large traditional homes on rolling terrain, next to Hillcrest Country Club.

pr-beverlywood.b: Beverwil Drive to Robertson, Castle Heights to National
pr-beverlywood.d: Beverlywood: a planned 1940s neighborhood of single-family homes with its own homeowners association and design rules.

pr-core.b: Pico Boulevard to Cadillac, La Cienega to Beverwil
pr-core.d: Pico-Robertson: walkable streets of duplexes, Spanish homes and apartments around Pico's kosher markets and shops.

palms-n.b: National Boulevard to Palms Boulevard, Sepulveda to Motor
palms-n.d: North Palms: apartments and small single-family streets near the Expo Line, between Westwood and Culver City.

palms-s.b: Palms Boulevard to Venice Boulevard, Sepulveda to Motor
palms-s.d: South Palms: dense apartment blocks and single-family pockets close to downtown Culver City.

mv-hill.b: Venice Boulevard to National, Centinela Avenue to Sepulveda
mv-hill.d: Mar Vista Hill: single-family streets on the slope with long views.

mv-west.b: Venice Boulevard to National, Walgrove Avenue to Centinela
mv-west.d: Mar Vista west of Centinela: single-family streets near Venice and the Mar Vista Farmers Market.

mv-south.b: Venice Boulevard to Washington, Sepulveda to Walgrove
mv-south.d: Mar Vista south of Venice Boulevard: smaller lots, many new builds and remodels, close to Culver City and Venice.

ven-ocean-front.b: The beach to Pacific Avenue and Main Street, Venice Boulevard to the Santa Monica line
ven-ocean-front.d: Venice's Ocean Front Walk and the walk streets: beach-close homes and buildings, many on car-free walk streets.

ven-oakwood-west.b: Main Street and Abbot Kinney to 6th Avenue, California Avenue to the Santa Monica line
ven-oakwood-west.d: North Venice between Main and Sixth: small lots of cottages, remodels and modern new builds near Rose Avenue.

ven-oakwood-east.b: 6th Avenue to Lincoln Boulevard, California Avenue to the Santa Monica line
ven-oakwood-east.d: Oakwood: Venice's historic working neighborhood, now a mix of original bungalows and new modern homes.

ven-windward.b: Pacific Avenue to Abbot Kinney, Brooks Avenue to Venice Boulevard
ven-windward.d: Windward Circle and the blocks around it: walk streets and homes between the beach and Abbot Kinney.

ven-canals.b: Pacific Avenue to Abbot Kinney, Venice Boulevard to Washington
ven-canals.d: The Venice Canals: homes facing the six canals and footbridges, plus the streets around them.

ven-milwood.b: Abbot Kinney to Lincoln, California Avenue to Washington
ven-milwood.d: Milwood: a quiet residential grid off Abbot Kinney of cottages and new builds.

ven-penmar.b: Lincoln Boulevard to Walgrove, Superba Avenue to the Santa Monica line
ven-penmar.d: Penmar: Venice east of Lincoln near Penmar Park and golf course, with larger lots than west Venice.

ven-east-south.b: Lincoln Boulevard to Walgrove, Venice Boulevard to Superba
ven-east-south.d: East Venice south of Superba: single-family streets.

wch-kentwood.b: Manchester Avenue north to the bluffs, Loyola Boulevard to Sepulveda
wch-kentwood.d: Kentwood: a 1940s and 1950s tract of single-family homes near Loyola Marymount, with ocean-close weather.

wch-loyola-village.b: Manchester Avenue to Westchester Parkway, Lincoln to Sepulveda
wch-loyola-village.d: Loyola Village: post-war single-family streets south of Manchester near Westchester Park.

wch-westport.b: Manchester Avenue north to the bluffs, Sepulveda to Airport Boulevard
wch-westport.d: Westport Heights: single-family streets on the bluffs east of Sepulveda with views toward the city.

wch-osage.b: Manchester Avenue south, Sepulveda to Aviation
wch-osage.d: Westchester east of Sepulveda: single-family streets and apartments between the town center and the airport.

mdr-peninsula.b: The strip between the ocean and the main channel, south of Venice
mdr-peninsula.d: Marina Peninsula: walk streets and beach homes between the sand and the marina channel.

mdr-silver-strand.b: The streets between Via Marina and the Ballona channel
mdr-silver-strand.d: Silver Strand: a small grid of homes and townhomes beside the marina's south jetty.

mdr-harbor.b: The marina's moles and Admiralty Way
mdr-harbor.d: Marina del Rey Harbor: high-rise and mid-rise apartments and condos on the moles around the small-craft harbor.

pdr-lower.b: The flats between Ballona Creek and the bluffs near Vista del Mar
pdr-lower.d: Lower Playa del Rey: beach-close streets and lagoon views at the foot of the bluffs.

pdr-upper.b: The bluff-top streets above Vista del Mar
pdr-upper.d: Playa del Rey's bluffs: view homes along the ridge above the beach and Ballona Wetlands.

pv-west.b: Playa Vista west of the central park, around Bluff Creek
pv-west.d: Playa Vista's west side: newer condos, townhomes and single-family homes along the bluff and Bluff Creek trail.

pv-east.b: Playa Vista east of the central park, around Millennium Drive and the Runway
pv-east.d: Playa Vista's east side: the Runway shops, office campuses and newer condos and townhomes.

cc-downtown.b: Downtown Culver City around Culver Boulevard and Main Street
cc-downtown.d: Downtown Culver City: restaurants, theaters and Sony Pictures, with condos and apartments nearby.

cc-arts.b: Along Washington and National near La Cienega
cc-arts.d: The Arts District and Hayden Tract: galleries, creative offices and a few residential blocks.

cc-carlson.b: The single-family streets around Carlson Park east of downtown
cc-carlson.d: Carlson Park: Spanish and traditional homes on a tree-lined grid a few blocks from downtown.

cc-veterans.b: The streets around Veterans Memorial Park and Overland Avenue
cc-veterans.d: Veterans Park area: single-family streets near the park, the plunge and the Culver City High campus.

cc-studio-village.b: Studio Village west of Overland near Jefferson
cc-studio-village.d: Studio Village: post-war single-family homes on quiet streets near the Ballona Creek path.

cc-sunkist.b: Sunkist Park in the city's west end
cc-sunkist.d: Sunkist Park: single-family streets in the west end near the 405.

cc-fox-hills.b: Fox Hills around the mall and Slauson
cc-fox-hills.d: Fox Hills: condos and apartments on the hills near Westfield Culver City.

cc-culver-west.b: Culver West, the unincorporated and city streets west of the 405 near Washington
cc-culver-west.d: Culver West: single-family streets near Culver West Park and Washington Boulevard.

cc-culver-crest.b: Culver Crest, the hillside above Overland and Jefferson
cc-culver-crest.d: Culver Crest: hillside homes with city and ocean views, above the Ballona Creek flats.

cc-blair-hills.b: Blair Hills, by the Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook
cc-blair-hills.d: Blair Hills: a hillside tract next to the Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook and its stairs.

weho-west.b: Santa Monica Boulevard south to the city line at Beverly, Doheny Drive to La Cienega
weho-west.d: West Hollywood West: a quiet grid of Spanish homes, duplexes and new builds next to the Pacific Design Center and Robertson.

weho-norma.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Sunset, Doheny Drive to San Vicente
weho-norma.d: Norma Triangle: small streets of cottages and duplexes in the triangle below Sunset, a short walk to both the Strip and Santa Monica Boulevard.

weho-strip.b: The West Hollywood side of Sunset Boulevard, Doheny to Crescent Heights
weho-strip.d: The Sunset Strip: the boulevard itself and the city's thin band of hillside lots just above it.

weho-center.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Sunset, San Vicente to La Cienega
weho-center.d: Central West Hollywood: apartments, condos and small homes around Santa Monica Boulevard's busiest stretch.

weho-north.b: Santa Monica Boulevard to Sunset and the city line, La Cienega to Fairfax
weho-north.d: West Hollywood north of Santa Monica Boulevard: historic courtyard buildings, condos and homes around Havenhurst, Harper and Kings Road.

weho-south.b: Santa Monica Boulevard south to the city line, La Cienega to Fairfax
weho-south.d: West Hollywood south of Santa Monica Boulevard: Spanish duplexes, small homes and new builds up to the city line near Melrose.

weho-east.b: Fairfax Avenue to the city line at La Brea
weho-east.d: West Hollywood's Eastside: apartments and condos around Plummer Park and the Formosa and Gardner streets.

fx-melrose.b: Melrose Avenue north to the West Hollywood line, Fairfax to La Brea
fx-melrose.d: The blocks just north of Melrose: Spanish duplexes and homes between the shopping street and West Hollywood.

fx-beverly-fairfax.b: Melrose Avenue to 3rd Street, Fairfax to La Brea
fx-beverly-fairfax.d: Beverly-Fairfax: 1920s and 1930s Spanish homes and duplexes around the Grove, the Farmers Market and Pan Pacific Park.

fx-plb.b: 3rd Street to 6th Street, Fairfax to La Brea
fx-plb.d: Park La Brea: the large apartment community and the residential blocks east of it toward La Brea.

mm-north.b: 6th Street to Wilshire Boulevard, Fairfax to La Brea
mm-north.d: Museum Row: LACMA, the Academy Museum and the La Brea Tar Pits, with apartments and condos north of Wilshire.

mm-south.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Olympic, Fairfax to La Brea
mm-south.d: Miracle Mile: a historic district of 1920s and 1930s duplexes and homes south of Wilshire's museums.

bg-melrose.b: The West Hollywood line south to Beverly Boulevard, La Cienega to Fairfax
bg-melrose.d: The Beverly Grove blocks between Melrose and Beverly: Spanish homes, duplexes and new builds near the Melrose shops.

bg-burton.b: Beverly Boulevard south to the Beverly Hills line, La Cienega west
bg-burton.d: Burton Way and Cedars: condo buildings along Burton Way and blocks around Cedars-Sinai and the Beverly Center.

bg-core.b: Beverly Boulevard to Wilshire, La Cienega to Fairfax
bg-core.d: Beverly Grove: Spanish duplexes and homes around 3rd Street's shops and restaurants.

bg-carthay.b: Wilshire Boulevard to Olympic, La Cienega to Fairfax
bg-carthay.d: Carthay Circle: a historic district of curving streets and Spanish homes, plus the blocks around it.

bg-south-carthay.b: Olympic Boulevard to Pico, La Cienega to Fairfax
bg-south-carthay.d: South Carthay: a historic district of 1930s Spanish homes on a quiet grid.

hp-la-brea-hancock.b: Melrose Avenue to Wilshire, La Brea to Highland
hp-la-brea-hancock.d: La Brea-Hancock: Spanish and traditional homes on streets just west of Hancock Park, with apartments near the boulevards.
